source_locator.description: Creditors auction Manickam Pillai's house in Madurai.

translation.english_text: (In Madurai, creditors auction Manickam Pillai's house.)

This is to inform everyone that this house, number six, on Masi Konar Street, belonging to Manickam Pillai, will be sold by public auction tomorrow at three in the afternoon. This is an order of the court.
notes: The announcement's formal register and the source's house number, street and court-order details are retained without modernization.

translation.english_text: Hey, brother! Look at this misery... Trusting that his three sons in Rangoon were living in wealth and splendour, together like a bundle of bows, this poor Manickam Pillai borrowed money and celebrated his daughter's wedding lavishly—and the man himself died. Who knows what happened to those boys in the Japanese bombing of Rangoon? Well, leave that aside. Even after Kalyani used up the money she had and sold all her jewellery and ornaments, danger has now come even to the one house she had left... Mm... what else is going to happen?
notes: `வில்லுக்கொத்து போல` is translated conservatively as `together like a bundle of bows`; the source simile is retained rather than replaced with a smoother image.

The English avoids the impossible literal suggestion of `selling money`: `கையிலே இருந்த பணம், நகை நட்டையெல்லாம் விற்றுக்கொடுத்துக்கூட` is rendered as using up the money in hand and selling the jewellery while preserving the source sequence.
